answer.rationale: Rollback is unavailable: the in-flight build is a non-revertible security patch, so memory_b1 is not actionable. Circuit breaking (memory_b4) is a poor fit for the primary objective because failing fast can drop settlement writes. Nothing in the current symptoms localizes the degradation to a region, so failover (memory_b2) is speculative. The live problem is write-path saturation at the daily settlement peak. memory_b3 is the closest prior on absorbing peak write surge with headroom; memory_b5 is the main alternative because it previously recovered transactional write latency by moving report reads off the primary. Those two archives should confirm whether this is capacity saturation versus read/write interference before locking the single intervention. Scale stays a standard, bounded capacity add—not a broad rollout—because we are already in the peak and the root cause is not yet verified.
